posts.title: Jab We Met
posts.excerpt: I have watched this movie more than 30 times, and somehow I still find something in Aditya and Geet that stays with me.
posts.review:
Geet gives Aditya the open space he needed. She opens up about herself, and somehow that makes him feel comfortable enough to talk about what he is going through when they meet. Later, they bond because both of them reciprocate so naturally.

He was broken, cheated on and at one of the lowest points of his life, yet he still chose his morals. He was with her in fucking Ratlam, in his darkest phase, with so many setbacks, and he still decided to go all in and get her home. Somewhere along the way, he realised the beauty, aura, innocence, sweetness and purity that Geet carries.

I feel like he might have fallen in love with her even before she told him about Anshuman. I know this because at one point in my life, I used to think that people who came into my life during my lowest phases were some kind of sign from the universe that they were meant to love me. I know now that it was completely wrong. They were probably just sent to teach me some lessons. It's crazy how God knows everything.

And I do believe Aditya fell in love with her, but because he knew she loved someone else, he stopped himself. Instead, he worked on himself. It wasn't Geet who gave him the power to rebuild himself. She just listened to him and 'pakkaaved' him with her talks. She gave him the space to open up and find himself again.

And he trusted, loved and believed in her so much that he left her, hoping she would be fine with the guy she was in love with. Then, when he gets her back, he could have easily proclaimed his love and said, "I have grown, be mine." But even then, he chose to hear what she felt before entering her territory.

He chose to be humane instead of overpowering her.

He helped her recover and get back to her family yet again. And finally, she wisely chose Aditya over the guy who thought she was crazy and didn't even care enough to check whether the girl who had left everything for him was okay or not.

I have watched this movie more than 30 times, and honestly, I think I was searching for Aditya for a very long time.

It was only after watching 'BKU' that I realised that.

posts.title: Obsession
posts.excerpt: The first time I watched it, I saw it one way. The second time, it almost felt like a completely different movie.
posts.review:
It shows how anything in excess isn't good. The guy has feelings for her, and she gets to know it. That's how girls are, we just somehow know these things. She even asks him directly if he has feelings for her, but he gets flustered and says no. Then he wishes for her to become obsessed with him and fall deeply in love with him.

And that's where he gets the karma for asking for too much.

I could see all those little things girls do when they are in love, but because he wished for obsession instead of just normal love, she starts doing everything to an extreme.

I actually liked the ending. I feel like the guy could have gotten a second chance for the mistake he made, but then again, life isn't always fair. He dies in the end, and the girl, completely consumed by her obsession and rage, ends up killing her two friends. In all that trauma, the guy kills himself, and the wish that had turned into wrath and ruined the lives of four people is finally released. The girl who was possessed by that wish comes back to normal.

That was my insight when I watched the movie for the first time. But when I watched it again, I had a completely different perspective. It almost felt like I was watching a different movie altogether.

I do feel, though, that the way the storyline is presented makes it feel more like watching a vlog than an actual movie.

posts.title: Sexing the Cherry
posts.excerpt: I really liked this book, especially because the female lead stayed in my mind much more than anything else in it.
posts.review:
I really liked Sexing the Cherry. What stood out to me first was the time in which the story is set, seventeenth-century London. I wasn't really aware of how things were back then. I used to feel that because London is such a hyped city, things must always have been perfect there, but that was clearly not the case.

What stayed with me the most was the female lead. She is fierce, bold and very open. She knows herself well and always takes a stand for herself. She is honest and bold, especially for a time when women were so suppressed.

The book has disturbing and harsh realities, but she is bold enough to voice herself every time. Even though she didn't really have financial freedom, she still felt independent, and I think that is what made me admire her so much.

Later, the story moves to Jordan's point of view, and he too seems to understand his mother more with time. He also falls in love with a girl, though I honestly don't remember that part very clearly. Maybe that is because I was so amazed by the female lead that she remained the strongest part of the book for me.

posts.title: The Liberation of Sita
posts.excerpt: I had never really come across our mythological stories from the female point of view before this, and that is what made this book stay with me.
posts.review:
I was amazed while reading this book. I had never really come across our mythological stories from the female point of view, and I was genuinely happy with how this was brought about.

This is a very individualistic topic, but I really loved how Sita Mata interacted with these women and how their point of view was narrated.

Starting with Surpanakha, I myself had always assumed that she was the villain. But while reading her story, she seemed so naive to me. Yes, it was her mistake to approach a man who was already married, but I don't think that should have led to her losing her beauty. I don't believe external beauty is everything, but women carry immense beauty in their physical appearance. People have often considered it a weakness or a form of allurement, but that is also simply a part of who she is. Women carry beauty along with great strength, emotional intelligence and empathy.

Then comes Ahalya, whose mistake seemed to be her beauty. Her husband was a sage, yet he didn't trust her enough before cursing her.

Next was Renuka, Parashurama's mother. I had never heard much about her before reading this book. I felt it was unfair of her son to follow his father blindly. Until then, I had respect for Parashurama. I agree that we are all human and learn things with time, but that act was something I really did not expect from such an educated and skilled man.

Then there was Urmila. Before this book, I only knew that she gave her sleep for her husband, but the things she went through were way beyond what I had imagined.

The author brought each of these women's perspectives out very well. Through them, Sita slowly understands that she does not have to be the ideal woman when things are really not favouring her. She does not have to keep proving herself or survive in this world by sacrificing everything, including herself.

The journey of learning about oneself, taking a stand for oneself and not being dependent on anyone is what I learnt through this book.

posts.title: Bethehelem Kudumba Unit
posts.review:
I usually avoid love stories for obvious reasons, and this movie in particular was recommended by a friend. But I had already read so many negative reviews about it on Reddit that I started reconsidering whether I should watch it at all. I eventually just gave it a try.

And fell hardest for it.

Just amazing!!! Even the smallest details have been captured so well, with so much thought behind them. Great casting, story, music, scenic shots and of course, all the references to older movies. I couldn’t catch most of them while watching, but after reading about them later, I realised how cleverly they had been included without ever pulling the story away from itself.

Nothing in the film felt far removed from reality it was more real than reel. The care put into it by the writer, director, producer, actors and everyone involved made it feel less like I was watching a constructed love story and more like I was listening to a believable, lovely and mature one unfolding somewhere in my own neighbourhood.

And for a generation with plenty of options, where relationships can unfold and turn into a mess so easily, this movie is really worth watching. It makes you realise that some things really do need time, maturity, understanding and patience.

posts.title: Hey Jude
posts.review:
The movie totally touched my heart. Nivin Pauly's another fine piece of art. The storyline is beautiful, it is perfectly paced. I was just reminded how we have time to understand ourselves but we end up losing ourselves to time, work, people or wealth. 

 My mother tongue is Konkani and we do visit Goa once in a year and this movie got me to live in Goa for about 2 hrs. And I lovee beaches and singling and music - I thoroughly felt like my family and I were living in Goa then and that's how our life has been going. It may seem exaggeration, but that's how I really felt. 

 Two learning from this movie would be - that everyone has their own flaws, we need to accept ours and others and move on. Only the people who have watched would really understand what I am stating here. Another one being, give yourself time, do whatever you feel like and be yourself - you need not change for anyone. 

Again, the storyline, cast, music, direction and screenplay were perfect! Even the way the movie was shot was so good the locations, lighting, colours, camera work and the way even simple scenes were captured. Do watch the movie with light heart because it will definitely get you drenched in emotions.

posts.title: The Bell Jar
posts.review:
On my journey of reading books written by women author to understand what and how they think and live, the first book I stumbled upon was this.

I was told why her when you can reading something better but I am sentimental and I deeply wished to understand a part of her sufferings at least through her work. I was disturbed! 

The books starts on a light note and slowly unveils the harsh reality. The audacity of people to not understand each other is crazy, I do hurt people but knowing they are mentally unstable I would not try to say something that would disturb them but here she was victim of a heinous act that made me wonder, how many more took advantage of the situation? 

The way she didn't think twice before putting in every details of things she went through amazed me. I wasn't aware of so many things, I learnt it through her. It is 2026 and still people take mental health very lightly and it is serious matter. I dont know how are we humans and the most intelligent specie on this earth when we cannot understand each other.

mediaEntries.title: Chasing Waves: My 2026 Beach Diaries
mediaEntries.text:
I have always preferred beaches over mountains, although I love both equally. Over the years, I've visited many beaches, and somehow, I still never seem to get over them. Every beach has something different to offer, and no matter how many I visit, the excitement of seeing the sea never really fades.

There is something about the beach that makes me forget everything else. The cool breeze, a beautiful sunset painting the sky in shades of orange, yellow, pink and blue, a good playlist playing in the background, and waves gently brushing against your feet as they reshape the sand beneath them. Honestly, heaven has its own little address!

In 2026, I got to visit beaches across Mumbai, Goa and Kerala. Each had its own character, charm and experience. But if I had to rank them based on beauty and cleanliness, one beach would undoubtedly take the crown.

## 1. Cabo de Rama Beach, Goa

My absolute favourite!

Cabo de Rama Beach was easily the highlight of my beach visits this year. When I first saw it from the top, I genuinely felt as though I had landed somewhere abroad. The crystal-clear water, the beautiful coastline and the relatively fewer visitors made the entire place feel exotic.

The beach sits below a viewpoint, and you have to make your way down a flight of steps to reach it. But the moment you see that stretch of blue from above, your excitement just keeps building with every step. I literally felt like jumping straight down (haha! Thankfully, I had enough sense not to).

The water is incredibly clear, but don't let its inviting appearance fool you. It gets deep, and entering the sea can be risky if you aren't a confident swimmer. There is also a smaller section of water along the side where non-swimmers can enjoy the surroundings more safely, while still exercising caution.

There are a few little spots and fancy decorative elements at the top that make for some lovely aesthetic pictures too.

What I loved most was how untouched and peaceful the place felt. It wasn't crowded, the surroundings were beautiful, and for those few hours, I could have easily forgotten I was still in India.

If there is one beach I would happily revisit, this is it!

## 2. Kerala: Golden Sand Beach and Kovalam

Kerala had a different kind of coastal beauty to offer.

I visited Golden Sand Beach as part of the Poovar backwater cruise. The boat ride itself was quite expensive for an hour, but the experience made up for it. The mangroves, backwaters and eventually the beach made the entire journey worthwhile.

We weren't allowed to enter the water when we visited, but that didn't take away from the experience. The golden sand, powerful waves crashing against the shore and the cool breeze made the beach look absolutely majestic.

There was also a resort connected to this stretch, with floating rooms, restaurants and even vendors selling tender coconuts from boats! That was something I found particularly interesting. Unfortunately, we were running late and couldn't explore that part.

I also visited Kovalam Beach during our trip to Thiruvananthapuram. Kerala's coastline really does have its own personality, and I would love to explore more of it.

## 3. Calicut Beach: The Afternoon Calm

This photograph is from Calicut Beach, which I happened to visit during the afternoon, around 3–4 PM.

It was relatively calm at that time, with the waves rolling in and plenty of space to enjoy the view. But apparently, the beach has a completely different personality later in the evening!

After that, it gets packed with people. There are plenty of food stalls and fun activities along the beach, making it a lively place to spend an evening.

I quite enjoyed seeing this quieter side of it. Sometimes, the best way to experience a place is to visit it before the crowds arrive.

## 4. Mumbai: Versova over Juhu?

A little Mumbai nostalgia!

I visited a Mumbai beach after quite some time. Whenever I used to visit Mumbai, Juhu Beach was usually my regular stop. This time, however, I visited Versova, and surprisingly, I found it considerably cleaner than Juhu.

I understand that Juhu faces its own challenges, given the number of people visiting it, but seeing the condition of the beach, especially during early mornings or evenings, can be quite disappointing.

Versova had food stalls too, so there was still plenty to explore. The road nearby was undergoing repairs and construction, with improvements intended to make travelling easier and faster.

It was nice to revisit Mumbai's coastline, but this time discover a different beach instead of returning to my usual one.

## A little more love for the waves

Every beach had something different to offer. Some gave me crystal-clear water and breathtaking views, some had golden sand and powerful waves, while others offered the simple pleasure of sitting by the shore and watching the world go by.

But Cabo de Rama definitely won my personal ranking this year!

And, of course, a special mention to the person who made these little adventures possible. **Funded by Dad.** ❤️

Here's to more sunsets, sandy feet, seashells, spontaneous trips and many more beaches to cross off the list!
mediaEntries.alt: A scrapbook-style collage of beach visits in Mumbai, Goa and Kerala in 2026

mediaEntries.title: On kindness, boundaries & moving on
mediaEntries.text:
I've had this same opinion for a long time. But they got access to our lives because we allowed them to, so I don't think they are completely at fault either.

I've been told several times that I tend to view the world the way I view myself, and I think that is exactly why I've been betrayed on several occasions. I understood what that meant eventually. Being too kind, warm and soft with the wrong people can lead to unnecessary pain and scars that stay with us for a lifetime.

But I also believe we have to forgive them and focus on ourselves. If God, who is superior to all of us, forgives our sins and gives us another day to unlearn, learn and relearn, then who are we to hold on to these trivial matters forever?

And honestly, holding on to feelings from the past can hurt our present more than the people who caused them ever did. To me, that is a bigger blunder than letting these people into our lives in the first place.

I actually appreciate that such people exist in our lives because they teach us that being too kind can also be injurious. There has to be a balance. Sometimes we keep committing to things forever simply because we are constantly thinking about everyone else. But these people teach us that it is okay to take a stand for yourself before anybody else.

There's one catch, though. These ruthless people should have the ability to understand and imbibe the kindness they receive, but most of them never will. And honestly, that's their loss. Because without learning that, they can never really build stable, long-term relationships with people.

We learn, we understand, and we move ahead. That's all.

There's so much more I could add to this. I'll probably add it someday soon.
